I implement AI in the corp space. So I'll tell you exactly how to tell if "We're coming for you." because it's how we calculate opportunities: 1) Is the job documented well. Basically can an AI always work out what to do. If the number is 80% yes, thats a tick. If you 'follow process', if you have written procedures, you are low hanging fruit. 2) Is your team composed of many people all doing the same thing. AI replacing people is only economical when we can remove multiple FTE's at once. In an insurance company we implemented a claims system. They had 1000 claims consultants. The great bulk of that work evaporated. They fired nobody, they just waited for them to leave or move them to work elsewhere. That projects capex was 500k. It returned millions per year. Nobody is spending 500k to remove 'one guy'. Specifically teams generally only minimize down to 3 people. Without going in to tons of detail on task automation, if you are a process worker in a team where multiple people do the same thing you have a red flag on your career. Learn to do things which are not documented, OR, work out how to use AI to automate the process before a consultant finds the role.
